'''Alperen Şengün''' ({{IPA|tur|ˈaɫpeɾæn ˈʃæɲɟyn}},{{Listen| filename = XXXXX |title =  XXXXX's voice |type = speech |description = recorded XXDATEXX }} born 25 July 2002) is a Turkish professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also represents the senior [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkish national team]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Best NBA Players From Turkey |url=https://www.ranker.com/list/famous-basketball-players-from-turkey/ranker-nba |access-date=19 May 2022 |website=ranker.com |date=19 May 2022}}</ref> Known for his post skills and creative playmaking abilities, Şengün was selected with the 16th overall pick in the first round of the [[2021 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Iko |first=Kelly |title=Jaylen Wells' screen navigation, Alperen Şengün's improved footwork: The IkoSystem |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5984383/2024/12/11/jaylen-wells-alperen-sengun-ikosystem/ |access-date=11 July 2025 |website=The New York Times |date=11 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lerner |first=Danielle |date=January 30, 2024 |title=How Rockets center Alperen Şengün is using fancy footwork to take the NBA by storm |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/alperen-sengun-footwork-highlights-rockets-18635520.php |access-date=January 30, 2024 |website=www.houstonchronicle.com}}</ref> He was named to his first [[NBA All-Star Game]] in 2025.
{{Listen| filename = XXXXX |title =  XXXXX's voice |type = speech |description = recorded XXDATEXX }}

==Early life and youth career==
Şengün was born on 25 July 2002<ref name="fiba1"/><ref name="yg"/> in [[Giresun]], a city in northeastern Turkey, to Kemal Şengün, a fisherman and former point guard who played in Turkey's first division in the late 1980s, and Ayşe Şengün. Although his parents wanted him to pursue swimming, he developed an appreciation for basketball after watching his older brother play. Şengün started to play basketball at the age of eight and trained in both basketball and swimming; however, due to the limited time available to train in both, he chose basketball.<ref name="bf1"/>

===Youth career: Giresun University and Banvit (2012–2019)===
In 2012, Şengün began playing youth basketball with teams affiliated with the sports club of [[Giresun University]],<ref name="m1"/> where he remained until 2014.<ref name="yg"/>

After being scouted by head coach Ahmet Gürgen during a youth sports festival, Şengün moved to [[Bandırma]], in northwestern Turkey, where he signed a youth contract with [[Bandırma B.İ.K.|Banvit]] on 19 August 2014.<ref name="bf1"/><ref name="gg"/> During the 2018–19 season, while playing for Banvit's under-19 team, Şengün won the Turkish Basketball Youth League championship, which had been established in 2017. He was also named the league's [[Most valuable player|MVP]].<ref name="s1" />

==Professional career==

===Bandırma Kırmızı (2018–2019)===
Şengün began his professional [[Sports club|club]] career during the 2018–19 TBL season with [[Bandırma Kırmızı B.K.|Bandırma Kırmızı]], a team competing in the second-tier [[Türkiye Basketbol Ligi|Turkish First League]] (TBL). Over 29 games, he averaged 10.8 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 21.9 minutes per game. He shot 47.6 percent from the field overall, including 53.6 percent on two-point attempts, 25.9 percent from three-point range, and 60.0 percent from the free-throw line.<ref name="proballers">{{cite web |title=Alperen Sengun, Basketball Player |url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/175107/alperen-sengun |website=Proballers |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

===Teksüt Bandırma (2019–2020)===
For the [[2019–20 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2019–20 BSL season]], Şengün joined [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Super League]] (BSL) club [[Teksüt Bandırma]], a club in the top-tier [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Super League]]. In 22 league games, he averaged 5.0 points and 3.9 rebounds in 13.5 minutes per game. He recorded a field goal percentage of 51.1 percent overall, including 57.5 percent on two-point attempts, 0-for-10 from three-point range, and 58.6 percent from the free-throw line.<ref name="proballers" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen Sengun – 2019-20 Season |url=https://www.tblstat.net/player/3076/1920 |website=TBLStat.net |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

He also competed in the [[FIBA Basketball Champions League]], one of Europe's secondary-level club competitions. During the [[2019–20 Basketball Champions League|2019–20 BCL season]], he appeared in 15 games, averaging 6.6 points and 3.3 rebounds in 14.9 minutes per game. He shot 48.0 percent from the field overall, including 53.6 percent on two-point attempts, 31.6 percent from three-point range, and 63.6 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen SENGUN at the Basketball Champions League 2019-20 |url=https://www.championsleague.basketball/19-20/player/Alperen-Sengun |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

===Beşiktaş (2020–2021)===
In August 2020, Şengün signed a three-year contract with the Turkish club [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]].<ref>{{cite web |date=7 August 2020 |title=Alperen Şengün Beşiktaş'ta |url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/79270/alperen-sengun-besiktasta.html |access-date=8 August 2020 |work=bjk.com.tr |language=tr}}</ref> He had an outstanding regular season, averaging 19.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.7 blocks in 28.3 minutes per game across 29 appearances in the [[Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen Sengun – 2020-21 Season |url=https://www.tblstat.net/player/3076/2021 |website=TBLStat.net |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref> On 12 May 2021, he was named the BSL Most Valuable Player for the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title= Alperen Sengun named Turkish BSL 2020-21 season MVP |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/tbl/1205414/alperen-sengun-named-turkish-bsl-2020-21-season-mvp/ |website=Eurohoops.net |date=12 May 2021|access-date=13 May 2021}}</ref> On the same day, he announced his decision to enter the [[2021 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Johnathan |date=12 May 2021 |title=Alperen Sengun, No. 14 basketball prospect in ESPN Top 100, to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31432025 |access-date=13 May 2021 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Over the course of the [[2020–21 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2020–21 BSL season]], Şengün averaged 18.6 points, 8.9 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.5 blocks in 28.1 minutes per game across 34 appearances. He shot 62.6 percent from the field overall, including 66.7 percent on two-point attempts, 21.2 percent from three-point range, and 81.2 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen Şengün – Türkiye Basketbol Federasyonu |url=https://www.tbf.org.tr/ligler/bsl-2020-2021/basketbolcu-detay/260291 |website=tbf.org.tr |access-date=27 January 2024 |language=tr}}</ref> Şengün also competed with Beşiktaş in the [[FIBA Europe Cup]], a fourth-tier European-wide competition. During the [[2020–21 FIBA Europe Cup|2020–21 season]], he appeared in three games, averaging 23.0 points, 7.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.7 steals, and 2.0 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game. He shot 71.0 percent from the field overall, including 75.9 percent on two-point attempts, 0–2 from three-point range, and 69.4 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen SENGUN at the FIBA Europe Cup 2020-21 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/20-21/player/Alperen-Sengun |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2021–present)===

====2021–22 season: Rookie season====

[[File:Alperen Şengün Houston Rockets vs Cleveland Cavaliers 2021-12-15 (51761119748) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Şengün during his rookie season with the Rockets in December 2021]]

Prior to the [[2021 NBA draft]], Şengün was projected to be a potential lottery draft pick but was ultimately selected outside the lottery with the 16th overall pick by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. The Thunder had acquired the 16th pick from the [[Boston Celtics]] as part of a trade that sent [[Kemba Walker]] to Oklahoma City in exchange for [[Al Horford]], [[Moses Brown (basketball)|Moses Brown]], and a 2023 second-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=NBA.com |date=June 18, 2021 |title=Celtics trade Kemba Walker, picks to Thunder |url=https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-trade-kemba-walker-picks-to-thunder |website=www.nba.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fortier |first=Marc |date=June 18, 2021 |title=Celtics Trade Kemba Walker to Oklahoma City |url=https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/celtics-trading-kemba-walker-to-oklahoma-city-report/2409101/#:~:text=The%20Celtics%20are%20also%20giving,round%20pick%2C%20sources%20tell%20ESPN.&text=June%2018%2C%202021-,It's%20a%20bold%20move%20by%20Brad%20Stevens%2C%20his%20first%20since,bruise%20in%20the%20same%20knee. |website=www.nbcboston.com}}</ref> Shortly after selecting Şengün, the Thunder traded his draft rights to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for two future first-round picks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rockets acquire 16th pick Alperen Sengun in trade with Thunder |url=https://www.nba.com/news/rockets-acquire-16th-pick-alperen-sengun-in-trade-with-thunder |access-date=31 July 2021 |website=NBA.com |date=21 September 2022}}</ref> On 7 August 2021, he signed a contract with the Rockets.<ref name=Hollinger>{{cite web |last=Hollinger |first=John |title=2021 NBA draft: A high lottery pick hiding in Turkey? Scouting Alperen Sengun and other international players to know |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2547988/2021/04/28/2021-nba-draft-a-high-lottery-pick-hiding-in-turkey-scouting-alperen-sengun-and-other-international-players-to-know/ |access-date=27 January 2024 |website=The Athletic |date=28 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Joshi |first=Hiren |title=Rockets Sign Josh Christopher and Alperen Sengun |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-josh-christopher-and-alperen-sengun |access-date=8 August 2021 |website=NBA.com |date=6 August 2021}}</ref>

====2022–23 season: Improving as a sophomore====

[[File:1_alperen_sengun.jpg|thumb|Şengün with the [[Houston Rockets]] in 2023]]

At the beginning of the offseason, the [[Houston Rockets]] traded [[Christian Wood]] to the [[Dallas Mavericks]], creating an opportunity for Şengün to be a starter. However, head coach [[Stephen Silas]] selected [[Bruno Fernando]] as the starting center, with him as a rim protector.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |date=19 October 2022 |title=Rockets likely to begin season with Bruno Fernando starting at center |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2022/10/19/rockets-likely-to-begin-season-with-bruno-fernando-starting-at-center/ |access-date=19 October 2022}}</ref> Fernando had a patellar tendinitis injury in his left knee early in the season, and in his absence, Şengün was promoted to the starting lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Coty M. |date=2 November 2022 |title=Alperen Sengun Credits Trust For Rockets Success As Starter |url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/news/alperen-sengun-houston-rockets-success-as-starter-jalen-green-kevin-porter-jr-stephen-silas |access-date=2 November 2022}}</ref> On 26 November 2022, he recorded 21 points, seven assists, and a then-career-high 19 rebounds in a 118–105 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/lists/takeaways-rockets-blast-thunder-on-career-nights-by-jalen-green-alperen-sengun/|title=Takeaways: Rockets blast Thunder on career nights by Jalen Green, Alperen Sengun|website=USA Today|last=DuBose|first=Ben|date=26 November 2022|access-date=12 January 2023}}</ref> On 6 December 2022, in a 132–123 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Şengün became the youngest center in NBA history to record at least 1,000 points and 200 assists at 20 years and 133 days old, surpassing [[Brad Daugherty (basketball)|Brad Daugherty]]'s previous record of 21 years and 153 days old.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alperen Sengun youngest center with 1000 points and 200 assists in NBA history |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1429865/alperen-sengun-youngest-center-with-1000-points-and-200-assists-in-nba-history/ |access-date=6 December 2022 |website=Eurohoops.net |date=6 December 2022}}</ref>

On 11 January 2023, Şengün recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 10 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 135–115 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]], becoming the youngest player in [[Houston Rockets]] history to achieve a triple-double in a game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pagaduan |first=Jedd |date=11 January 2023 |title=Alperen Sengun reaches heights not even Hakeem Olajuwon could reach in Rockets' loss to Kings |url=https://clutchpoints.com/rockets-news-alperen-sengun-reaches-heights-not-even-hakeem-olajuwon-could-reach-in-loss-to-kings |access-date=11 January 2023 |website=ClutchPoints}}</ref> On 16 January 2023, he posted a season-high 33 points, along with 15 rebounds, six assists, and four blocks in a 140–132 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=LeBron drops 48, Lakers beat Rockets 140-132 to snap skid |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401468819 |access-date=17 January 2023 |website=ESPN |date=17 January 2023}}</ref> He became the youngest player in [[Houston Rockets]] history to record at least 30 points and 10 rebounds in a game, surpassing the previous record set by [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] in 1984. He also became the youngest center in NBA history to record at least 30 points, 15 rebounds, and five assists in a game, breaking [[Shaquille O'Neal]]'s record set in 1993.<ref>{{cite news |last=Shapiro |first=Michael |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/rockets-alperen-sengun-hakeem-olajuwon-17722782.php |title=Alperen Sengun breaks records held by Hakeem Olajuwon, Shaq |newspaper=Chron |date=17 January 2023 |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref> On 25 January 2023, Şengün recorded his second career triple-double with 21 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 108–103 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]]. He became the youngest center in NBA history to record multiple triple-doubles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/rockets-news-alperen-sengun-notches-epic-triple-double-record-not-even-nikola-jokic-matched|title=Rockets center Alperen Sengun notches epic triple-double record not even Nikola Jokic matched|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=25 January 2023|access-date=25 January 2023}}</ref> On 7 April 2023, he recorded a season-high 21 rebounds, along with 14 points in a win against the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alperen Sengun had his rebounding career-high with 21 against Charlotte |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1487004/alperen-sengun-houston-rockets-charlotte-hornets-nba-career-high/ |access-date=27 January 2024 |website=Eurohoops.net |date=8 April 2023}}</ref> He also led all centers aged 20 or younger in assists per game, surpassing his own mark from his rookie season.<ref>{{Cite tweet |author=Bradeaux |user=BradeauxNBA |number=1644370550695907339 |title=Most assists per game for a center 20 or younger in NBA History: 3.9 — Alperen Şengün (This season); 3.6 — Chris Webber (1993-94); 2.6 — Alperen Şengün (2021-22); 2.5 — Demarcus Cousins (2010-11); 2.4 — Nikola Jokić (2015-16). |retweet=Bradeaux [Twitter]}}</ref>

Şengün started in 72 out of 75 games he played, with averages of 14.8 points, 9.0 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game. He shot 55.3 percent from the field and averaged 28.9 minutes per game. His sophomore campaign drew praise from NBA stars: [[Kevin Durant]] liked his game;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Easton |first=Ed Jr. |title=Kevin Durant appreciates talent of young Rockets center Alperen Sengun |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2023/01/31/kevin-durant-appreciates-talent-of-young-rockets-center-alperen-sengun/ |access-date=27 January 2024 |website=USA Today |date=31 January 2023}}</ref> [[Paul George]] compared his passing and rebounding to [[Magic Johnson]], [[Pau Gasol]], and [[Nikola Jokić]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=Villas |first=Rexwell |date=11 April 2023 |title='Some Magic type s**t': Paul George's eye-popping Alperen Sengun take will hype Rockets fans |url=https://clutchpoints.com/rockets-news-paul-george-eye-popping-alperen-sengun-take-will-hype-fans |access-date=20 July 2023 |website=clutchpoints.com}}</ref> and [[Anthony Edwards (basketball)|Anthony Edwards]] said the Rockets should build around Şengün.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barefield |first=Brian |date=11 January 2023 |title=Timberwolves sing praises of Alperen Sengun after playing Rockets |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2023/01/11/timberwolves-sing-praises-of-alperen-sengun-after-playing-rockets/ |website=USA Today |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

====2023–24 season: Breakthrough====

==National team career==

===Junior national team===
Şengün competed with the [[Turkey men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team|Turkish under-16 national team]] at the [[2018 FIBA Under-16 European Championship]], which was held in [[Novi Sad]], Serbia. In the competition, he won the bronze medal. Şengün was also selected to the competition's [[2018 FIBA U16 European Championship#Awards|All-Tournament Team]]. In seven games played with an average of 24.9 minutes, he recorded 14.4 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.6 steals, and 1.4 blocks per game. He shot 56.9 percent from the field overall, including 61.9 percent on two-point attempts, 22.2 percent from three-point range, and 48.6 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen SENGUN at the FIBA U16 European Championship 2018 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2018/player/Alperen-Sengun |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

He played a role on the Turkish under-17 national team that competed at the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], which was held in [[Argentina]]. Turkey ultimately finished in fifth place.<ref name="yg"/><ref name="bf1"/><ref name="st1"/> In seven games with an average of 28.6 minutes, he averaged 15.9 points, 12.3 rebounds, and 2.0 assists. He shot 58.3 percent from the field overall, including 64.1 percent on two-point attempts, 12.5 percent from three-point range, and 56.5 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen SENGUN at the FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup 2018 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2018/player/Alperen-Sengun |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

Şengün also played at the [[2019 FIBA Under-18 European Championship]], with the [[Turkey men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Turkish under-18 national team]], which won the tournament's silver medal. He was also selected to that [[2019 FIBA U18 European Championship#Awards|competition's All-Tournament Team]], being the only Turkish player that was chosen for that honor.<ref name="eh1"/> In seven games played at that tournament, he averaged 11.9 points, 9.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.6 steals and 1.7 blocks in 23.0 minutes per game. He shot 54.5 percent from the field overall, 59.2 percent on two-point field goal attempts, 16.7 percent on three-point field goal attempts and 59.5 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alperen SENGUN at the FIBA U18 European Championship 2019 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2019/player/Alperen-Sengun |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

===Senior national team===
[[File:Alperen Şengün.png|thumb|Şengün with the Turkey national team in 2020]]
In November 2020, Şengün joined the senior [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkish national team]], as he played with Turkey at the [[2022 EuroBasket Qualifiers]]. In four games played at the qualifiers, he averaged 12.0 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 blocks in 23.1 minutes per game. He shot 53.3 percent from the field overall, 51.9 percent on two-point field goal attempts, 66.7 percent on three-point field goal attempts and 50 percent from the free-throw line.<ref>{{cite web |title=FIBA EuroBasket 2022 Qualifiers |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/qualifiers/player/Alperen-Sengun |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=27 January 2024}}</ref>

In September 2022, Şengün played at [[EuroBasket 2022]]. He was the best player on the team, leading the team in points (16.8 per game) and rebounds (8.2 per game).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Turkey at the FIBA EuroBasket 2022 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/team/Turkey |access-date=11 September 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref> Şengün and Turkey were eliminated in the round of 16 after losing to [[France men's national basketball team|France]] in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 September 2022 |title=Gobert saves France from elimination, Les Bleus outlast Turkey in OT |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/news/gobert-saves-france-from-elimination-les-bleus-outlast-turkey-in-ot |access-date=11 September 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball}}</ref>

On August 29, 2025, Şengün recorded 22 points, 11 rebounds, 9 assists, and 2 blocks in Turkey's 85–70 win over the [[Czech Republic men's national basketball team|Czech Republic]] in the second Group A match of [[EuroBasket 2025#Preliminary round|EuroBasket 2025]], narrowly missing a triple-double by one assist. On September 3, in the final Group A match, Şengün led Turkey to a 95–90 win over [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]], finishing with 28 points, 13 rebounds, and 8 assists to secure first place in the group. On September 9, he finally recorded his triple double (19 points, 12 rebounds, 10 assists) and became the youngest player ever to record a triple-double in [[EuroBasket]] history, as Turkey defeated [[Poland men's national basketball team|Poland]] in the quarterfinals. On September 12, 2025, Turkey overwhelmed [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greece]] during the semifinals with a 68–94 win where he tallied 15 points, 12 rebounds, and 6 assists. On September 14, 2025, during the [[EuroBasket 2025 final|finals]], Şengün recorded 28 points, 3 rebounds, 3 assists, and one block during an 83–88 loss against [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]], led by [[Franz Wagner]] and [[Dennis Schröder]], securing the silver medal, his second since 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 September 2025 |title=EuroBasket 2025: Alperen Sengun lifts Turkey into semifinals |url=https://www.nba.com/news/eurobasket-2025-day-12-recap |access-date=9 September 2025 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He was selected for the “all-star five” team for his distinguished performance in the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 September 2025 |title=All-Star Five: Schroder, Doncic, Wagner, Antetokounmpo, Sengun |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/all-star-five-schroder-doncic-wagner-antetokounmpo-sengun |access-date=15 September 2025 |website=fiba.baskeball}}</ref>
